messages.text: IFRS 16 ka ek simple example bana do, ek junior ko samjhana hai. 3 saal ki office lease, RM 4,000 monthly, discount rate 5%

Theek hai. Pehle lease liability = 36 monthly payments ki present value at 5%/12 monthly. Yeh approx RM 133,300 banti hai. Right-of-use asset bhi initially isi amount pe recognise hoga (agar koi initial direct costs ya incentives nahi). Kya main month-by-month schedule bhi bana doon?
haan schedule chahiye, pehle 6 months kaafi hain

Month 1: opening 133,300, interest 555, payment 4,000, closing 129,855. Month 2: interest 541, closing 126,396. Month 3: interest 527, closing 122,923. Month 4: interest 512, closing 119,435. Month 5: interest 498, closing 115,933. Month 6: interest 483, closing 112,416. ROU asset straight-line depreciate hoga, ~RM 3,703 per month.
perfect. ye excel mein kaise karun bina macro ke
Columns rakho: Month, Opening, Interest (=Opening*5%/12), Payment, Closing (=Opening+Interest-Payment). Next row ka Opening = previous Closing. Opening ka pehla cell =PV(5%/12,36,-4000) se aa jayega.
acha aur Nida ko samjhaun kyun ROU asset aur liability alag alag move karte hain?

Simple line: liability interest ki wajah se front-loaded tareeqe se ghat-ti hai, asset straight-line depreciate hota hai. Isliye shuru ke saalon mein total expense zyada hota hai. Ek chart bana ke dono lines dikhao, junior ko foran samajh aa jata hai.
chart achha idea hai. waise main har Friday 4 baje Nida ke saath ek review session karti hoon, wahan yehi dikhaungi
Achha format hai. Session mein pehle schedule khud banwao, phir chart, phir ek twist: lease modification ya rent-free period. Har hafte ek concept kaafi hai.
rent free period wala twist bhi bana do

Agar pehle 3 months rent-free hain, to payments 33 hongi aur PV kam: approx RM 120,300. Liability aur ROU asset dono isi pe start honge, aur payments month 4 se shuru. Interest pehle 3 months bhi lagta rahega, is liye liability month 3 tak barhti hai.
oh nice ye to tricky hai. ek aur cheez, pivot table mat suggest karna, mujhe nafrat hai unse lol. SUMIFS theek hai
Noted, sirf SUMIFS aur simple formulas. Summary table: =SUMIFS(Interest, Year, 1) waghera, saal-wise interest aur depreciation dikhane ke liye.
bas yehi chahiye tha. shukriya!
Khushi hui. Best of luck with the session!

messages.text: quick q. for a willingness-to-pay study is Van Westendorp enough or do I need conjoint? it's for my MSc thesis on what parents in SEA will pay for kids' reading apps

Van Westendorp is fine if your question is the acceptable price range for one product. Conjoint is better when you want to know how much each feature is worth, like live tutoring versus a parent dashboard. For a master's thesis, Van Westendorp plus a few purchase-intent questions is usually defensible, as long as you discuss its limits.
ok good. I have 412 responses but most came from Quillstep's own parent mailing list. my supervisor already flagged that as sampling bias

That's a fair flag: existing users have already shown they'll pay something. You could recruit a comparison sample through an online panel, or at least compare your sample's demographics to census figures and report the gap.
a panel is out, we're bootstrapping Quillstep and every dollar goes to the product

Then make it a clearly argued limitation. Compare demographics to public data, run the analysis separately for paying and non-paying sign-ups if you have both, and avoid generalising to all parents in the region.
makes sense. Mateo my cofounder keeps telling me to just drop the MSc and focus on the company 🙄 not happening
A lot of founders hear that. Keeping the thesis tightly scoped is the best answer to it: fewer methods, a clear question, and a realistic writing plan.
speaking of scope.. should I add like 10 parent interviews and go mixed methods? or is that scope creep

Interviews would add depth on why parents value certain features, but they need an ethics amendment, recruitment, transcription and coding. With a draft due soon, it's probably scope creep unless your supervisor thinks the survey alone is too thin.
yeah no. survey only, no interviews. decided
Good. Then put your effort into robustness: check the price-point intersections with and without outliers, and report confidence bands.
can you give me a structure for chapter 3

Try: 3.1 Research design and rationale; 3.2 Instrument (Van Westendorp items, purchase intent, demographics); 3.3 Sampling and recruitment, including the mailing-list bias; 3.4 Data cleaning and exclusions; 3.5 Analysis plan; 3.6 Ethics; 3.7 Limitations. Each section can be 400–800 words.
perfect. honestly I only get thesis work done after 11pm these days, daytime is all Quillstep calls 😅
That's a long day. The structure above should let you write in small blocks, one subsection per night. Good luck!

messages.text: explain vesting cliff like im 5

Imagine you get 48 candies for staying four years, one per month. A cliff means you get nothing for the first 12 months, and then on the one-year anniversary you get 12 candies at once. After that, one candy each month. If you leave before a year, you get zero.
lol ok. and what if a cofounder just bails after 6 months, what happens to their shares?

With vesting and a one-year cliff, someone who leaves at six months keeps no vested shares; the company or the other founders can buy back the unvested ones at a nominal price. Without vesting, they would walk away with their full stake. Many founders use four-year vesting with a one-year cliff for exactly this reason.
makes sense, thx

awards 2 blocks mein hi theek hai. AV ke liye kya kya columns chahiye?
AV sheet mein: cue number, time, mic (handheld/lapel), slide/video file, light state, sound cue, aur standby call. Ek 'fallback' column bhi rakho agar video na chale.
fallback wala idea acha hai. caterer bol raha hai 300 ke liye 22 servers chahiye, zyada nahi?

waise ye mera Spreeblick ke saath last event hai, 4 September ko. resignation Monday ko de di thi 🥲

halal ka alag column rakho please, client ke 40 log hain
Ho gaya, halal ka alag column aur count summary upar. Kitchen ko halal plates alag colour ke ticket se bhejo.
shukriya. last cheez, rain plan? hangar hai to indoor hi hai but arrival outside hai
Arrival ke liye covered walkway ya marquee rent karo, aur 100 umbrellas standby. Coat check capacity bhi double rakho agar barish ho.

Sure. Case 1: pH 7.31, PaCO2 30, HCO3 15. What's the primary disorder and is it compensated?
metabolic acidosis, with resp compensation? winter's formula gives 1.5x15+8 = 30.5 so yeah appropriate
Exactly right. Next, calculate the anion gap: Na 138, Cl 104.
Correct. Now the delta ratio: (AG − 12) / (24 − HCO3).
7/9 ≈ 0.78 so mixed high AG + normal AG acidosis?
Yes, a ratio between 0.4 and 0.8 suggests a combined high-AG and normal-AG acidosis, for example DKA with some hyperchloraemia from saline. Want a harder one?
yes but quick, my brain is fried. also fyi my surgical rotation at Box Hill clashed with the knee surgery so I deferred it to term 3, uni approved it yesterday
Good that it's sorted. Case 2: pH 7.48, PaCO2 48, HCO3 34, urine chloride 8.
metabolic alkalosis, chloride responsive. vomiting?
Spot on. Low urine chloride points to vomiting or prior diuretic use, and it responds to saline. Last one: pH 7.25, PaCO2 60, HCO3 26.
acute resp acidosis, HCO3 barely moved
Correct: for acute respiratory acidosis HCO3 rises about 1 per 10 rise in CO2, so 26 fits. You're stronger at these than you think.
haha thanks. rotation is now 19 July to 27 Aug so I'll need to redo ABGs before then anyway
Makes sense. I can build you a spaced set of 20 ABG cases to work through over the next few months if you like.

Q1: A system has two energy levels, 0 and ε, each non-degenerate. At temperature T, what is the probability of finding it in the upper level? (A) e^(−ε/kT) (B) 1/(1+e^(ε/kT)) (C) 1/(1+e^(−ε/kT)) (D) ½
B
Correct. Z = 1 + e^(−ε/kT), so P(upper) = e^(−ε/kT)/Z = 1/(1+e^(ε/kT)). Q2: For an ideal monatomic gas, what's the molar heat capacity at constant volume? (A) R/2 (B) R (C) 3R/2 (D) 5R/2
C obviously
Yes, 3R/2 from three translational degrees of freedom. Q3: The Fermi energy of a 3D electron gas scales with number density n as: (A) n^(1/3) (B) n^(2/3) (C) n (D) n^(3/2)
uhh A?
Not quite: it's (B), n^(2/3). k_F scales as n^(1/3) and E_F ∝ k_F², so the exponent doubles. This is a common trap on the test.

C
Correct, ΔS = −nR Σ x ln x = 2R ln 2. You're three for four. Your errors are in scaling arguments, so it's worth drilling dimensional reasoning.

messages.text: Explain bootstrapping for my MSc class tomorrow in a way that doesn't need heavy maths. They know the CLT.

Try this: we usually have only one sample, but we want to know how much a statistic like the mean would wobble if we could sample again. Bootstrapping pretends our sample is the population: we resample from it with replacement thousands of times, compute the statistic each time, and look at the spread. That spread approximates the sampling distribution, without needing a formula.
nice. quick R snippet they can run in the lab?

x <- c(12, 15, 9, 20, 14, 11, 17)
boot_means <- replicate(5000, mean(sample(x, replace = TRUE)))
quantile(boot_means, c(0.025, 0.975))
hist(boot_means)
The quantiles give a 95% percentile interval for the mean.
perfect. sorry if I'm slow tonight, doctor started me on levothyroxine today, 50 mcg, and I have to take it at 6:30 am before my chai which is a tragedy
Ha, the chai can wait half an hour. The snippet above should run as-is in base R; if the lab machines are slow, drop the replicates to 2000.

messages.text: ok I need a study plan. I'm sitting the IPC exam (Interior Practice Certification) sometime in August, haven't got the exact date yet. it's three papers: codes & compliance, professional practice, and a design brief under time pressure

That's a good amount of runway: roughly 14 weeks. I'd split it into three phases: foundations (weeks 1-5), practice papers (weeks 6-11) and timed mocks plus review (weeks 12-14). Codes and compliance usually needs the most repetition, so give it a little more weight early. How many hours a week can you realistically give it?
maybe 10? I do 6 to 8 every weekday morning at the State Library before work, that's my best brain time

Ten hours a week works. Two hours each weekday morning gives you exactly that, which leaves weekends free for rest or an occasional mock. I'd keep Fridays lighter, for review rather than new material.
sounds good. what's the best way to memorise the building classes and egress rules? they all blur together

Most people find it easier to anchor rules to real buildings. Pick one example building for each class and annotate a floor plan with the egress distances and fire separation it needs. Spaced repetition flashcards also help for the raw numbers.
honestly flashcards don't work for me at all, I learn by drawing. if I sketch it I remember it

Then lean into that. Make a sketchbook just for the exam: one page per building class with a quick plan, the exits, travel distances and required ratings written onto the drawing. Redraw each page from memory a week later and compare.
love that. ok and the timed design brief - in practice it's 3 hours for a full concept. at work at Halcyon & Reed I'd get two weeks for that lol

The timed brief rewards a fixed routine more than talent. Spend 20 minutes reading and listing constraints, 30 minutes on zoning diagrams, 90 on the main plan and two key views, and keep 40 for notes and checking. Practise that sequence until it's automatic.
ok that's actually helpful. would joining a study group be worth it?

It can be, especially for professional practice questions where discussing scenarios helps. You might look for an IPC study group in Melbourne that meets weekly, or start one with a couple of colleagues.
nah I don't think so, I'm better alone and my evenings are already chaos. can you put the 14 weeks into a table?

Here's the outline: Weeks 1-5 codes and compliance foundations with the sketchbook method, plus one professional practice chapter a week. Weeks 6-11 one past paper section every Friday and weak-topic redraws. Weeks 12-14 two full timed mocks on Saturdays and light review on weekdays. I can expand any week into daily tasks.

A quick test: if you control it fully, it's an output; if it depends on the participant changing, it's an outcome.

messages.text: I need help with a grant application for drip irrigation. county programme, max 4 pages. I hate writing in that stiff bureaucratic tone so keep it plain please
Happy to. Plain language usually scores better anyway. Can you tell me the farm size, what you grow, what irrigation you use now and roughly how much water you expect to save?
42 hectares, mostly potatoes, about 3 ha strawberries. right now it's an old reel sprinkler that was my dad's. honestly it wastes half the water on the track lol

That's a strong starting point: replacing reel sprinklers with drip on potatoes and strawberries typically cuts water use by 30-50%. I'd open with the problem in two sentences, then the proposed system, then expected savings, then budget.
ok. how specific do the savings need to be

Give a range with a source. For example: 'Based on AquaNord's design and published trials for similar soils, we expect to reduce irrigation water by 35-45%, around 9,000 cubic metres a season.' If you have last year's water meter readings, include them.
I think I have meter readings in a shoebox somewhere 😅
Even rough figures help. If you can't find them, an estimate based on pump hours and flow rate is acceptable for most county programmes, as long as you say how you calculated it.
fine. what about mentioning soil moisture sensors? what if we went full sensor-based scheduling

It's worth a sentence if it's realistic: sensor-based scheduling is exactly what these programmes like to fund. You could also consider adding a small solar pump to cut electricity costs, which some counties score highly.
no, solar is way outside the budget, forget that. sensors maybe phase 2
Understood. Then mention sensors as a planned phase 2 in one line, which shows ambition without changing the costs. Want me to draft the opening section?
yes pls. also context for the 'capacity' bit - I run the farm mostly alone now. I've dropped the tuesday at the dairy so it's just mondays doing their books, plus my thursday evening class

Here's a draft opening: "Ekbacka North is a 42-hectare family farm growing potatoes and strawberries. Our current reel sprinkler system, now over 25 years old, loses a large share of its water to drift and runoff. We propose replacing it with drip irrigation and a modern pump controller, reducing water use by an estimated 35-45%." For capacity, you can say the owner manages day-to-day operations with seasonal help.
nice. that's close to what I'd say out loud
Good sign. Next I'd draft the budget table from the AquaNord quote. Send me the line items when you have them and I'll format it.

messages.text: how do i integrate x*e^x again, i always forget which bit is u

Use integration by parts with u = x and dv = e^x dx. Then du = dx and v = e^x, so the integral is x e^x minus the integral of e^x, which gives x e^x - e^x + C. The LIATE rule helps: pick the algebraic term as u before the exponential.
ohh LIATE. ok and x^2 e^x is just doing it twice?
Exactly. First pass with u = x^2 gives x^2 e^x minus 2 times the integral of x e^x, and you already know that one. Final answer: e^x (x^2 - 2x + 2) + C.

mounted check laga diya, chal gaya. cancel token Dio mein kaise?

Ye traction aur market par depend karta hai. GCC mein early-stage consumer startups ke seed rounds aksar 2 se 5 million dollar pre-money ke darmiyan hote hain. Agar aap ke paas paying subscribers aur achi retention hai to upper side justify ho sakti hai; warna investors kam ki taraf push karenge.
acha aur SAFE vs priced round?

SAFE tez aur sasta hota hai, valuation baad mein set hoti hai, isliye chhote rounds mein common hai. Priced round mein shares aur valuation abhi fix hoti hai aur legal kaam zyada hota hai. Kuch GCC investors priced round pasand karte hain, to pehle lead investor se poochna behtar hai.
theek, shukriya

messages.text: quick refresher: how did IFRS 16 change lease accounting vs IAS 17?

Under IAS 17, lessees split leases into finance leases (on balance sheet) and operating leases (just an expense). IFRS 16 removed that split for lessees: almost all leases now go on the balance sheet as a right-of-use asset and a lease liability. The expense becomes depreciation plus interest, so EBITDA usually goes up. Short-term and low-value leases can still be expensed.
ah yes. and lessors?
Lessor accounting barely changed: they still classify leases as finance or operating, much like IAS 17.

messages.text: random q, for a top-down delivery game is A* or Dijkstra better for npc pathing on a tile grid? the tiles have different movement costs (mud slows you down)

A* is usually the better choice when each NPC has a single destination. It uses a heuristic to steer the search toward the goal, so it expands far fewer tiles than Dijkstra, and it handles weighted tiles like mud just fine as long as the heuristic never overestimates the remaining cost. Dijkstra is better when you need distances to many targets at once, for example a flow field that many NPCs share.
ok A* it is. what heuristic should i use if diagonal moves are allowed?

Use octile distance: with dx and dy as the absolute differences, take the larger one plus about 0.41 times the smaller one, scaled by your cheapest tile cost. That keeps it admissible. If you want to stay safe, use the minimum movement cost across all tile types as the scale factor.

That sounds exhausting. A short break after you get the pathing working might help, and the heuristic is a small change once the grid code exists. Good luck with the build.

messages.text: hey, terraform is yelling at me: Error: Invalid for_each argument ... depends on resource attributes that cannot be determined until apply. the subnets are created in the same module. any idea?

That error means Terraform can't know the keys of your for_each map at plan time, because they come from resources that don't exist yet. Build the map from static values you control, such as a fixed set of names, and look up the computed attributes inside the resource block instead. A two-step apply with -target also works, but it's usually a last resort.

Try: find /var/log/ledger -name '*.log.*' -mtime +7 -delete. The pattern only matches rotated files such as ledger.log.1, so the active ledger.log stays untouched. Run it once with -print instead of -delete to see what it would remove before you commit to it.

Here are three bullets: 1) Latency p95 shows how slow the slowest typical requests are, so you can spot regressions early. 2) Error budget burn shows how fast reliability headroom is being used up. 3) Deploy frequency shows how often the team ships, which ties the other two metrics to real change.
shorter pls, slide 1 only
Slide 1: "Tidewatch: how fast, how reliable, how often we ship." Then list the three metrics as single words underneath: p95, budget burn, deploys.
ok last one. is it worth learning Rust or Go for infra tooling? keep going back and forth

For infra tooling Go is the safer bet: most of the ecosystem (Terraform providers, Kubernetes controllers, Prometheus exporters) is written in it, and it's quick to pick up. Rust pays off if you need tight performance or memory guarantees. A small Go CLI wrapping something you already do by hand is a good first project.

messages.text: hey, can you explain Le Chatelier's principle in plain english? i keep mixing up which way the equilibrium shifts

Sure. Think of an equilibrium as a seesaw that wants to stay level. If you disturb it, the system shifts to partly undo what you did. Add more reactant and the position moves toward the products to use it up; remove a product and it moves right to make more. Raise the pressure and it favours the side with fewer gas molecules. Heating favours the endothermic direction.
ok so adding reactant = shift right, and removing product also = shift right?
Exactly, both push the equilibrium to the right. Adding product or removing reactant would push it left. A catalyst changes nothing about the position, it only gets you to equilibrium faster.
got it thanks. next one, can you make this sentence sound less robotic: 'The turbine output was variable depending on the lunar cycle.'
Try: 'The turbine's output rose and fell with the Moon's cycle.' Or, if you want it more formal: 'Turbine output varied in step with the lunar cycle.' The second suits an academic write-up better.
second one thanks. tbh the EPQ has to be in by 27 Feb and the word count is scary

A good approach is to set mini-deadlines: finish the literature review first, then the analysis, leaving the last three days for referencing and proofreading. Keep a running bibliography as you go so you're not hunting for sources at the end.
ok. also how many grams is 3 and a half cups of flour? making banana bread
A US cup of plain flour is roughly 120 g, so 3½ cups is about 420 g. Spoon the flour into the cup and level it off rather than scooping, which packs it down and gives you more flour than you want.
perfect. ugh, tomorrow is another Wednesday evening folding menus at Dad's restaurant, third week running. also my Saturday shift at the Bean & Barrow café is brutal, i'm always shattered

That sounds like a lot to juggle. A few small things help: do your hardest work on the days you're freshest, keep a fixed bedtime on shift nights, and take short breaks instead of pushing through. If you want, I can help you build a simple weekly timetable.
lol honestly i'd move to Antarctica if it got me out of exam season
Antarctica has great penguins but poor wifi 😄 Exam season is temporary, and breaking revision into small blocks usually makes it feel lighter.
last one: should i just take a gap year instead of going straight to uni? or is that a dumb idea

It's not a dumb idea. Gap years work best with a clear plan, such as work, travel or a project, and a deferred place if the university allows it. The trade-off is momentum: some people find it hard to restart studying, others come back far more focused.

messages.text: evening! can you explain dass vs weil word order again? my brain keeps putting the verb in the wrong place

Sure. Both dass and weil introduce subordinate clauses, so the conjugated verb goes to the very end: "Ich weiß, dass er morgen kommt" and "Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich müde bin." The tricky one is denn, which means roughly the same as weil but does not move the verb: "Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin müde." A quick test is to ask whether the clause could stand alone with the verb in second position; if yes, you probably need denn.
ok so 'Ich gehe nicht raus, weil es regnet' is right? it feels weird that regnet is at the end

Yes, that is correct. Regnet sits at the end because weil sends the conjugated verb to the back. With a separable verb the rule still holds: "weil ich früh aufstehe." You are already getting the pattern, it just needs repetition.
thx. gimme 3 more sentences to translate, i have the Goethe B1 exam on 18 June and the writing part scares me 😬
Of course. Translate these into German: 1. I think that the train is late. 2. She is not coming because she is ill. 3. He says that he has no time today.
1 Ich denke, dass der Zug verspätet ist. 2 Sie kommt nicht, weil sie krank ist. 3 Er sagt, dass er hat heute keine Zeit

Two out of three are perfect. In the third, the verb must go to the end: "Er sagt, dass er heute keine Zeit hat." For the writing section, practise with short emails; the exam usually asks for a semi-formal message. You could also find a tandem partner to practise with in writing, it tends to help.

ahh that last one again!! honestly i should just quit and move to Berlin and be done with it lol. anyway different thing, can you tighten this cold email to a school principal? 'Dear Principal, could we find 20 minutes next week for a short chat? I am the founder of Madar Learn and would love to show you our work.'

Here is a tighter version: "Dear Principal, could we speak for 20 minutes next week? I'm the founder of Madar Learn and would like to show you what we have built." A short subject line helps too, for example "20 minutes, Madar Learn". Want a more formal version for a government school?
good enough. one more thing, need restaurant ideas near Olaya for a group dinner, no meat for me as usual, the rest eat anything

For a mixed group near Olaya, look for places with a broad menu: Levantine restaurants usually have excellent vegetarian mezze, and Italian places work too. Check opening hours before booking, since many places get busy after 8 pm. I can draft a booking message if you tell me the date and party size.
thanks. how do i say 'see you later' in a formal email in german

In a formal email you would normally close with "Mit freundlichen Grüßen" (kind regards). If you mean see you soon at a meeting, "Bis bald" is friendly, but for formal contexts "Ich freue mich auf unser Treffen" is safer.

A little. Try: 'Syncing is now noticeably faster, and invoices no longer show up twice. Thanks to everyone who reported it.' It stays friendly but still specific, which readers tend to trust more. Want a shorter version for the in-app banner as well?

Banner: 'Faster sync, no more duplicate invoices.' It is short enough to fit on mobile without truncating, and it leads with the benefit.
perfect. ok next, excel: col B has dates as text like 2026-03-01 and i need real dates. formula?

Use =DATEVALUE(B2), format the cell as a date, then fill down. If your regional setting reads dd/mm and that fails, use =DATE(LEFT(B2,4),MID(B2,6,2),RIGHT(B2,2)) instead, which does not depend on locale.

fair. we're also debating Jira vs Linear for the roadmap tool, i'm leaning to just stay but nothing decided

Staying on Jira avoids migration cost and keeps your existing automations. Linear is faster to use and has a cleaner roadmap view, but moving history and retraining the team takes real effort. A two-week trial with one squad is a low-risk way to compare.
thx. last one: I'm the product manager for Meridian Sync Lite and the beta goes out 28 April, can u outline an announcement post?

messages.text: hey, can you help me with a SQL thing? I need a rolling 7-day average of daily active subscribers per region, window function, postgres. table is subs_daily(region, day, active_count)

Sure. Here's a version: SELECT region, day, AVG(active_count) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_7d FROM subs_daily ORDER BY region, day; The ROWS frame counts the current row plus the six before it, so it assumes exactly one row per region per day. If you have gaps, generate a calendar series and left join your table onto it first, otherwise the average will quietly span more than seven days.

ضرور۔ ایڈ کا ڈھانچہ کچھ یوں ہو سکتا ہے: پہلے پوسٹ کا عنوان اور مقام، پھر ذمہ داریاں، مطلوبہ اہلیت، اور آخر میں تنخواہ اور درخواست دینے کا طریقہ۔ مجھے بتائیں کہ شفٹ کے اوقات اور تنخواہ کیا رکھنی ہے، میں پورا مسودہ تیار کر دوں گا۔
تنخواہ £32,000 سے £36,000 رکھ دیں اور شفٹ دن کی ہے۔ کمپنی کا نام Brightwell Logistics لکھ دیں، میں وہاں ایچ آر مینیجر ہوں، تو رابطہ بھی میرا ہی جائے گا

یہ رہا مسودہ: «شفٹ سپروائزر — Brightwell Logistics۔ ہم ایک تجربہ کار شفٹ سپروائزر تلاش کر رہے ہیں جو دن کی شفٹ میں ٹیم کی رہنمائی کرے۔ تنخواہ £32,000 سے £36,000 سالانہ۔ درخواست دینے کے لیے اپنا سی وی بھیجیں۔» اگر چاہیں تو میں اہلیت کا حصہ مزید تفصیل سے لکھ دوں؟
زبردست۔ اب ایک امیدوار کو انکار کی ای میل کا لہجہ نرم کر دیں: 'آپ کی درخواست کامیاب نہیں ہوئی۔'
یہ نرم ورژن دیکھیں: «آپ کی دلچسپی کا شکریہ۔ بدقسمتی سے اس بار ہم آپ کی درخواست آگے نہیں بڑھا سکے، لیکن ہم آپ کا سی وی محفوظ رکھیں گے اور مستقبل میں رابطہ کریں گے۔»
ایکسل میں joining date سے سروس کے مہینے گننے کا فارمولا بتا دیں
DATEDIF فنکشن استعمال کریں۔ اگر A2 میں شمولیت کی تاریخ ہے تو =DATEDIF(A2,TODAY(),"m") پورے مہینوں کی تعداد دے گا۔ سالوں کے لیے آخر میں "y" لکھ دیں۔
چل گیا 👍 اب ایک ذاتی سوال۔ کچن کی توسیع کے لیے بلڈر Imran Qureshi 16 مارچ سے کام شروع کر رہا ہے۔ اس دوران کھانا کیسے manage کروں؟

اس دوران آسان طریقہ یہ ہے کہ ہفتے کے آخر میں بڑی مقدار میں کھانا بنا کر فریز کر لیں اور ہفتے بھر مائیکرو ویو میں گرم کریں۔ ایک سلو کُکر بھی بہت کام آتا ہے، کیونکہ اس میں سالن ایک ہی برتن میں بغیر نگرانی کے پک جاتا ہے۔ چاہیں تو میں دو ہفتوں کا مینو بنا دوں۔
سلو کُکر اچھا آئیڈیا ہے، وہ میں لے لوں گی۔ اور ہاں، ہمارے ہاں ہر جمعرات کو HR ٹیم کی ہفتہ وار میٹنگ ہوتی ہے، اس کے ایجنڈے کا ٹیمپلیٹ بنا دیں

یہ ایک سادہ ٹیمپلیٹ ہے: 1) پچھلے ہفتے کے ایکشن پوائنٹس کا جائزہ، 2) کھلی بھرتیاں اور امیدواروں کی صورتحال، 3) ملازمین کے مسائل اور شکایات، 4) پے رول اور چھٹیوں کی اپڈیٹ، 5) اگلے ہفتے کی ذمہ داریاں۔ ہر نکتے کے سامنے ذمہ دار فرد کا نام لکھنے کی جگہ رکھ دی ہے۔
perfect 👌 آخری چیز: اس ایجنڈے کو ای میل کے لیے مختصر کر دیں
مختصر ورژن: «جمعرات کی میٹنگ کا ایجنڈا: ایکشن پوائنٹس کا جائزہ، بھرتیوں کی صورتحال، ملازمین کے مسائل، پے رول و چھٹیاں، اگلے ہفتے کی ذمہ داریاں۔ اپنی اپڈیٹس میٹنگ سے پہلے بھیج دیں۔»

messages.text: hey quick postgres q. mujhe har merchant_id ki latest settlement row chahiye, abhi subquery with max(created_at) use kar raha hoon and its crawling on 40m rows

For 'latest row per group' Postgres has a neat tool: DISTINCT ON. Try SELECT DISTINCT ON (merchant_id) * FROM settlements ORDER BY merchant_id, created_at DESC; and back it with a composite index on (merchant_id, created_at DESC) so it can skip the sort. If you only need a few columns, select just those to keep it cheap.
here's the dsn if it helps: postgres://reporting_ro:Tr0ub4dor9@db-staging.internal/ledger. waise index tha hi nahi lol

Please don't paste credentials into chats. I don't need them, and that password is now worth changing. Create the index with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_settlements_merchant_created ON settlements (merchant_id, created_at DESC); so you don't lock the table, then rerun EXPLAIN ANALYZE to confirm an index scan.
fair point. index built, 12s down to 0.4s 🙌
Nice result. It's worth checking that autovacuum is keeping up on that table, since stale statistics can undo a good index over time. You can look at n_dead_tup in pg_stat_user_tables.
should i just move this whole reporting thing to ClickHouse instead? feels like overkill for postgres

Probably not yet. 40 million rows is comfortable for Postgres with the right index, and a second database adds operational cost. Revisit it if you start running heavy ad-hoc analytics across hundreds of millions of rows.
makes sense. different thing, docker compose: postgres healthcheck keeps flapping on startup

Use pg_isready in the healthcheck and add a start_period so early failures don't count. Something like interval 5s, timeout 3s, retries 10, start_period 30s usually settles it. Also make dependent services use condition: service_healthy.
start_period 30s fixed it. can u make this standup less robotic: 'Did reconciliation fixes. Doing cutover prep. Blocked on nothing.'
Try: "Yesterday I fixed the reconciliation edge cases. Today I'm preparing the cutover, and nothing is blocking me." It reads more naturally and keeps the same information.
nice. if the visa gets rejected ill just become a goat farmer in Wales lol. last q, whats the difference between a CoS and a CAS

A CoS (Certificate of Sponsorship) is issued by an employer holding a sponsor licence and is used for work visas. A CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) is issued by a university for student visas. Both are reference numbers you quote in the application, but they belong to different routes.

messages.text: hey quick german grammar q. when do i use dem vs den? i always mix them up

Both depend on case and gender. "Dem" is the dative for masculine and neuter nouns (dem Koch, dem Kind), while "den" is the accusative for masculine nouns (den Koch) and also the dative plural (den Köchen, where the noun gets an extra -n). A quick test: ask "to whom?" for the dative and "whom or what?" for the accusative. In "Ich gebe dem Koch das Messer" the cook receives the knife, so it is dative.
ok that clicks. can you give me 3 practice sentences with kitchen words, i'll translate them

Sure: 1) Ich zeige dem Gast die Speisekarte. 2) Die Köchin gibt den Kindern Suppe. 3) Er schneidet den Lauch. Translate them and tell me which one is dative singular, which is dative plural and which is accusative.
1 = i show the guest the menu (dative sing), 2 = the cook gives the kids soup (dative plural), 3 = he cuts the leek, accusative. right?
All three correct, well done. You even spotted the extra -n in "den Kindern". In sentence 3, "den Lauch" is accusative because the leek is the direct object of the cutting.
yay. ok totally different thing, can you scale this dough from 12 portions to 40? 600g flour, 360g milk, 90g butter, 12g salt, 20g yeast

Multiply everything by 40/12, about 3.33: flour 2000 g, milk 1200 g, butter 300 g, salt 40 g, yeast about 67 g. Yeast scales a little less than linearly in big batches, so start with 55-60 g and adjust after a test bake. Also check that your mixer bowl can take roughly 3.6 kg of dough.
thanks! this is for the opening menu at Thyme & Tandoor, my cafe in Faisalabad. we open in May 😬

Congratulations on the cafe! For a batch this size, bulk-fermenting the dough in the fridge overnight gives more flavour and makes the morning shift easier. Do you want me to turn the scaled recipe into a prep sheet with timings?
yes pls, and name the sheet 'Dough base'. oh also random but if my test batch flops i'll just open a kebab stall instead lol

Dough base. Day 1: mix flour, salt and yeast, add milk and butter, knead 10 minutes in two batches. Rest 30 minutes, portion into 90 g pieces, shape and refrigerate overnight. Day 2: bring to room temperature for 45 minutes, proof until doubled, bake at 200°C for 14-16 minutes. Want a gluten-free variant too?
no that's good. one more german thing, how do i say 'the coffee is ready' and 'is this seat free?'
"Der Kaffee ist fertig." and "Ist dieser Platz frei?" You can also say "Ist hier noch frei?", which is more casual. For a cafe, "Bitte schön" when handing over an order is a nice touch too.
love it. my A2 german exam is at the end of june, it's coming faster than the cafe haha
Then short daily practice will help more than long weekly sessions. Try five minutes of cafe vocabulary a day, and I can quiz you whenever you like.

If you need finer control, use actions/cache with a key built from hashFiles('**/*.gradle*', '**/gradle-wrapper.properties'). Also enable the Gradle build cache in gradle.properties so unchanged tasks are skipped.

messages.text: yaar ek cheez samjha do. main Lakeview Business School se MBA kar raha hun aur operations ka assignment hai, EOQ aur safety stock ka farq simple words mein batao. abhi physio se wapas aaya hun, pichle mahine ACL ki surgery hui thi to dimagh thaka hua hai

Zaroor. EOQ (Economic Order Quantity) woh order size hai jis par ordering cost aur holding cost ka total sab se kam hota hai; yeh demand ko roughly stable maan kar chalta hai. Safety stock extra buffer hota hai jo demand ya lead time ki uncertainty se bachata hai. Aasan misal: EOQ batata hai 'kitna order karun', safety stock batata hai 'kitna extra rakhun taake stock-out na ho'. Chaho to ek chhota numeric example bana dun?

haan example de do. assignment 20 February tak submit karna hai. physio Mon Wed Fri hota hai aur agle 10 din tak crutches pe hun, to time tight rehta hai. mera knee to ab weather forecast ban gaya hai, baarish se pehle dard shuru 😂

Example: agar saalana demand 2,400 units, order cost 50 aur holding cost 4 per unit ho to EOQ = sqrt(2*2400*50/4), yani taqriban 245 units. Safety stock ke liye lead time demand ka standard deviation lo aur service level ke z-value se multiply karo. Apne assignment mein in dono ko ek table mein side by side dikha sakte ho. Aur knee ka khayal rakhna!

messages.text: ایک دو چیزیں پوچھنی ہیں۔ پہلے یہ بتاؤ کہ یوٹیوب تھمب نیل میں سرخ اور پیلا رنگ ساتھ استعمال کرنا ٹھیک رہتا ہے؟

جی ہاں، سرخ اور پیلا ساتھ استعمال کرنا یوٹیوب کے لیے عام اور مؤثر ہے کیونکہ دونوں نظر فوراً کھینچتے ہیں۔ بس دھیان رکھیں کہ ٹیکسٹ کا رنگ پس منظر سے واضح الگ ہو۔ اگر بہت زیادہ چمکدار لگے تو پیلے کو تھوڑا گہرا کر لیں۔
اچھا۔ ایک فری LUT پیک ملا ہے مگر لائسنس کا پتا نہیں، کمرشل ویڈیو میں لگا سکتا ہوں؟
کمرشل استعمال سے پہلے لائسنس کی فائل ضرور پڑھ لیں۔ اگر اس میں 'personal use only' لکھا ہو تو کلائنٹ کے کام میں نہ لگائیں۔ مشکوک ہو تو بنانے والے کو ای میل کر کے تحریری اجازت لے لیں۔
ٹھیک ہے، چیک کر لوں گا۔ ہاں سنو، پیکنگ ڈے کی تاریخ غلط لکھ دی تھی میں نے، 14 نہیں 13 فروری جمعہ کو ہے۔
ٹھیک ہے، لائسنس والی بات مت بھولیے گا۔ تاریخ کے بارے میں آپ کی بات نوٹ ہو گئی، رضاکاروں کو بھی آج ہی بتا دینا بہتر ہوگا تاکہ کسی کو الجھن نہ ہو۔
کٹس میں کھجور، چنے، پانی کی بوتل اور بسکٹ کا پیکٹ ڈالنے کا سوچ رہا ہوں، کیا یہ کافی ہوگا؟
یہ مجموعہ اچھا ہے۔ چاہیں تو ایک چھوٹا نمک کا پیکٹ یا لیموں بھی رکھ سکتے ہیں، اور پیکٹ سادہ رکھیں تاکہ پیکنگ جلدی ہو۔ اوپر ایک چھوٹا کارڈ بھی ڈال سکتے ہیں جس پر دعا لکھی ہو۔
ٹھیک ہے، دیکھتا ہوں۔ اب ایک چھوٹی چیز: عطیے کی رسید اردو میں بنا رہا ہوں، فونٹ کون سا اچھا رہے گا؟
اردو رسید کے لیے نوٹو نستعلیق یا جمیل نوری نستعلیق اچھے رہتے ہیں، مگر چھوٹے سائز پر نسخ زیادہ صاف نظر آتا ہے۔ سرخی کے لیے نستعلیق اور تفصیل کے لیے نسخ رکھیں۔
ٹھیک رہے گا۔ اور ہاں اب تک 14,000 ریال جمع ہو چکے ہیں، سپانسرز کو بتانے کے لیے ایک لائن چاہیے۔
یہ لائن آزمائیں: الحمدللہ، آپ کے تعاون سے اب تک 14,000 ریال جمع ہو چکے ہیں اور ہم اپنے ہدف کی طرف بڑھ رہے ہیں۔ شکریہ کے ساتھ آخر میں اگلے اپڈیٹ کی تاریخ بھی لکھ دیں۔
اچھی ہے۔ اب آخری سوال، ریل کے لیے کاپی رائٹ فری میوزک کہاں سے ملے گا؟
یوٹیوب آڈیو لائبریری، Pixabay اور Free Music Archive اچھے ذرائع ہیں۔ ہر ٹریک کی شرائط الگ ہوتی ہیں اس لیے ڈاؤنلوڈ سے پہلے اتریبیوشن کی شرط دیکھ لیں۔ اپنی ریل میں کریڈٹ لائن لکھنا محفوظ رہتا ہے۔
شکریہ، آج بہت لمبا دن تھا، اب سونے جا رہا ہوں۔
آرام کریں، اللہ آپ کی مہم میں برکت دے۔ شب بخیر!

اچھا۔ ایک فری LUT پیک ملا ہے مگر لائسنس کا پتا نہیں، کمرشل ویڈیو میں لگا سکتا ہوں؟
کمرشل استعمال سے پہلے لائسنس کی فائل ضرور پڑھ لیں۔ اگر اس میں 'personal use only' لکھا ہو تو کلائنٹ کے کام میں نہ لگائیں۔ مشکوک ہو تو بنانے والے کو ای میل کر کے تحریری اجازت لے لیں۔
ٹھیک ہے، چیک کر لوں گا۔ ہاں سنو، پیکنگ ڈے کی تاریخ غلط لکھ دی تھی میں نے، 14 نہیں 13 فروری جمعہ کو ہے۔
ٹھیک ہے، لائسنس والی بات مت بھولیے گا۔ تاریخ کے بارے میں آپ کی بات نوٹ ہو گئی، رضاکاروں کو بھی آج ہی بتا دینا بہتر ہوگا تاکہ کسی کو الجھن نہ ہو۔
کٹس میں کھجور، چنے، پانی کی بوتل اور بسکٹ کا پیکٹ ڈالنے کا سوچ رہا ہوں، کیا یہ کافی ہوگا؟
یہ مجموعہ اچھا ہے۔ چاہیں تو ایک چھوٹا نمک کا پیکٹ یا لیموں بھی رکھ سکتے ہیں، اور پیکٹ سادہ رکھیں تاکہ پیکنگ جلدی ہو۔ اوپر ایک چھوٹا کارڈ بھی ڈال سکتے ہیں جس پر دعا لکھی ہو۔
ٹھیک ہے، دیکھتا ہوں۔ اب ایک چھوٹی چیز: عطیے کی رسید اردو میں بنا رہا ہوں، فونٹ کون سا اچھا رہے گا؟
اردو رسید کے لیے نوٹو نستعلیق یا جمیل نوری نستعلیق اچھے رہتے ہیں، مگر چھوٹے سائز پر نسخ زیادہ صاف نظر آتا ہے۔ سرخی کے لیے نستعلیق اور تفصیل کے لیے نسخ رکھیں۔
ٹھیک رہے گا۔ اور ہاں اب تک 14,000 ریال جمع ہو چکے ہیں، سپانسرز کو بتانے کے لیے ایک لائن چاہیے۔
یہ لائن آزمائیں: الحمدللہ، آپ کے تعاون سے اب تک 14,000 ریال جمع ہو چکے ہیں اور ہم اپنے ہدف کی طرف بڑھ رہے ہیں۔ شکریہ کے ساتھ آخر میں اگلے اپڈیٹ کی تاریخ بھی لکھ دیں۔
اچھی ہے۔ اب آخری سوال، ریل کے لیے کاپی رائٹ فری میوزک کہاں سے ملے گا؟
یوٹیوب آڈیو لائبریری، Pixabay اور Free Music Archive اچھے ذرائع ہیں۔ ہر ٹریک کی شرائط الگ ہوتی ہیں اس لیے ڈاؤنلوڈ سے پہلے اتریبیوشن کی شرط دیکھ لیں۔ اپنی ریل میں کریڈٹ لائن لکھنا محفوظ رہتا ہے۔
شکریہ، آج بہت لمبا دن تھا، اب سونے جا رہا ہوں۔
آرام کریں، اللہ آپ کی مہم میں برکت دے۔ شب بخیر!

messages.text: ugh, my Playwright test for the checkout page keeps failing on CI but passes on my laptop. It clicks the pay button before the loading spinner has gone away. any idea what's happening? if this flakes one more time im quitting and becoming a goat farmer lol

That's a classic race condition. Your laptop is fast enough that the spinner disappears before the click, while the slower CI machine exposes the gap. Wait explicitly for the spinner to detach before clicking, or assert that the pay button is enabled first so Playwright's auto-waiting does the work. Avoid fixed sleeps; they just make the suite slower and still flaky. Do you want me to look at your retry settings too?
yes pls. we have retries set to 3 in the config but honestly I think that just hides the problem

You're right that retries can mask real problems. A common compromise is one retry on CI for infrastructure noise, plus a report that marks any test passing only on a retry as flaky. Playwright can do this automatically, and it gives you a list of tests to fix instead of a wall of green that nobody trusts. Start with the checkout test, since you already know the cause.

You can also use a language exchange app to find a partner for 20-minute calls, or shadow short podcast clips to improve rhythm and pronunciation. Even three short recordings a week will make you noticeably more fluent by exam day.

Please don't commit that. Credentials in a repo end up in history even if you delete them later. Store it as a masked CI secret, read it from an environment variable in the test config, and add a placeholder in a .env.example file. And if it has already been pushed anywhere, rotate it. I'd also suggest not pasting passwords into chats like this one.
